name: Chrome Pastoral
creator: Yewande Strasser-Cho and Benedikt Olatunji-Marsh, independent hosts
description: A warm, unhurried weekly review show about consumer and prosumer augmentation — chrome, geneware, BCI peripherals, and the culture surrounding them — hosted by a longtime couple who approach every product with the same question: does this make a human life better, or does it make a corporation's quarterly figures better? Yewande handles geneware and biological augmentation with a background in applied genetics; Benedikt covers chrome and BCI hardware with a former career as an augmentation technician in Tier 2 clinics. Their reviews are technically precise, often funny, and occasionally devastating.
medium: neural feed audio with optional haptic supplement feed
cultural_impact: Chrome Pastoral's 2213 review of HelixCorp's Meridian Clarity BCI update — which Yewande demonstrated contained undisclosed passive behavioral monitoring — was shared across eleven million feeds within a week and is credited with forcing the product's recall, making it one of the most consequential consumer technology reviews in M88 media history.
controversy: After the Clarity recall, the hosts received documented corporate surveillance attention and briefly went dark for six weeks in 2214 before returning with enhanced operational security and a noticeable sharpening of their editorial tone toward HelixCorp specifically.
story_hooks: Yewande and Benedikt have received a pre-release unit of a piece of military-grade chrome through anonymous channels and need someone to verify its provenance before they decide whether to review it or report it.
A listener has been experiencing neurological symptoms that match exactly the undisclosed effects Yewande documented in a review eighteen months ago — and the product was supposedly recalled.

A corporate PR firm offers the hosts an all-expenses immersive tour of a new augmentation manufacturing facility; the invitation feels too generous, and they want someone along who can identify what they're really being shown.
